name: SLB
legalName: SLB Limited (EDGAR name: SLB LIMITED/NV; formerly Schlumberger Limited)
description: SLB is the world's largest oilfield services and equipment company: it does not own oil, it sells technology and services to the companies that do. Its customers (oil companies and national oil companies in more than 100 countries) pay for drilling services and tools, measurement and well evaluation, completions and production equipment, chemicals and artificial lift, and digital software and seismic data. Revenue is therefore driven by how much customers spend on drilling and production, especially internationally and offshore, not by the oil price directly. Full-year 2025 revenue was 35.7 billion dollars (down 2%); ChampionX (production chemicals and artificial lift), bought in an all-stock deal that closed in 2025, added 1.5 billion dollars and made Production Systems the largest segment. Q2 2026 revenue was 8,972 million dollars and net income 786 million, with Middle East disruptions offset by offshore growth in Latin America, Europe and Africa, and Asia. It commits to return more than 4 billion dollars to shareholders in 2026.

businessLines.name: Production Systems
businessLines.shareBasis: 13,325 of 36,648 million sum of segment revenue (consolidated revenue 35,708 million after eliminations and other)
businessLines.how: Equipment sales and long-term supply contracts plus recurring consumables and services (chemicals, replacement lift equipment) that follow the number of producing wells.
businessLines.description: Completions, artificial lift, production chemicals (from the ChampionX acquisition) and production equipment; segment detail beyond that not extracted.

businessLines.name: Well Construction
businessLines.how: Day-rate and per-job fees for drilling services and tools; volume tracks rig counts and drilling activity, and fell in 2025 in Mexico, Saudi Arabia and offshore Africa.
businessLines.description: Drilling services and tools, drill bits, drilling fluids and cementing.

businessLines.name: Reservoir Performance
businessLines.how: Fees per job and per service day from operators improving well productivity; international stimulation and evaluation activity slowed in 2025.
businessLines.description: Reservoir-centric services: evaluation and wireline, intervention and stimulation (pressure pumping for well productivity).

businessLines.name: Digital
businessLines.how: Software subscriptions and platform fees, digital operations service contracts, and licensing of a seismic data library to multiple customers; the highest-margin segment.
businessLines.description: Digital Operations, Platforms & Applications (software) and Digital Exploration (seismic data licensing) across the energy value chain.

margin.label: Company states 28% pretax operating margin FY2025, up 291 bps

businessLines.name: All other
businessLines.description: Businesses outside the four reported segments (not itemised in the excerpt read).

brands.name: ChampionX (production chemicals and artificial lift; acquired 2025 in an all-stock deal)
brands.share: 1.5 billion dollars of 2025 revenue, about 4.2% of 35,708 million (computed); ChampionX recorded about 3.4 billion of 2024 revenue excluding drilling technologies, so the full-year contribution will be larger in 2026
